The Koa Is an Off-Grid-Ready Camper Van With a Striking Walnut and Maple Interior Design
20 photos
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / Beachside Custom Vans
If you come up with the right layout and design, you can make a camper van almost as comfortable as a simple studio apartment. Today, I have just the right camper van to share with you to prove what I just said.
Meet Koa, a conversion based on a 2026 AWD Mercedes-Benz Sprinter with a 144" wheelbase and a high roof. It's the work of Beachside Custom Vans, a Jacksonville, Florida-based boutique camper van builder specializing in roam-ready mobile homes.
This Sprinter doesn't have that many exterior upgrades like we've seen on other vans. However, the ones it does have make it relatively obvious that you're looking at a camper .
For instance, a ladder on the driver's side offers quick and easy access to the roof. There, you'll come across a White Top Adventure rack that holds a 200 W solar panel. The roof also has a ProBreeze vent fan and a Victron A/C unit.
Beachside Custom Vans gets standard cargo vans from Mercedes, which come with no windows. The company adds them itself – this rig has two AM Auto half-slider windows, as well as two windows at the back.
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / Beachside Custom Vans Other notable mods are Dark Star Offroad side steps, power and water hookup points, and a set of flares.
Flares, also known as pods or capsules, are designed to increase the van width to allow you to fit a bed inside in an east to west arrangement instead of the standard north to south. This rig's fiberglass pods are finished in black, and the one on the passenger side has a half-slider window.
Inside is where the biggest transformation happened. Slide the door open, and a beautifully designed interior will greet you. It has an open layout, with no wall separating the driver's cabin from the living space. Moreover, the driver and passenger seats are mounted on factory swivel bases, so they can be turned around to face the back of the van.
Regarding aesthetics, the customer opted for Lonseal walnut and holly marine-grade vinyl flooring, wall panels upholstered in Marathon Plus oat-colored woven fabric, a matching ceiling, and a mix of maple and walnut cabinetry: maple for the lowers and walnut for the uppers. The look is completed by white solid surface countertops and three lighting zones.
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / Beachside Custom Vans Straight ahead as you enter, Beachside Custom Vans devised a single-person bench with a Lagun table mount. It offers a bit of storage space in the form of a cabinet with two shelves.
Next, we have the kitchen, which is split into two units. It features a Dometic NRX 115 fridge with a tiny freezer compartment, a humongous stainless steel sink with a cover that matches the countertop, a portable single-burner induction stove, a 4-in-1 oven, and a flip-up table that offers additional surface area. A ProBreeze vent fan is perfectly positioned above to draw out the smells and fumes from cooking.
Two overhead cabinets, a cutlery drawer, and two lower cabinets are available for storage in the kitchen. There's also a floor-to-ceiling unit on the driver's side that integrates a closet with hanging space, as well as three drawers.
The drawer on the bottom hides a Laveo dry-flush toilet – since the drawer has heavy-duty slides, you don't have to remove the toilet to use it. Just sit down and get to business.
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / Beachside Custom Vans In the rear, you get a fixed sleeping arrangement. It boasts a queen-size bed, three overhead cabinets, charging points, and a ceiling A/C unit.
Finally, the space underneath the bedroom serves as a garage. To make loading and unloading items easier, the builders added a pull-out tray attached to heavy-duty slides. They can support up to 500 lb. (227 kg).
The garage's sides are taken up by large boxes that accommodate the utility systems. Power is on the left side – the electrical system's highlights are two 200 Ah lithium batteries and a 3,000 W inverter.
Three charging sources can be used to keep the batteries topped off: solar power , shore power, and 50-amp DC-DC charging while the engine is running. If used right, you'll never run out of juice. Furthermore, a temperature sensor detects if the electrical box gets too hot, and turns on two fans (one on each end) to pump out the hot air.
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / Beachside Custom Vans As for plumbing, the van is equipped with a 35-gallon (132-liter) freshwater tank, an 11-gallon (41-liter) greywater tank with an electronic dump valve, a 4-gallon (15-liter) water heater, and an outdoor shower connection.
The "command center" for the rig's utilities is conveniently located in the kitchen, integrated into the side of the floor-to-ceiling unit I mentioned earlier. It includes standard and USB outlets, three dimmer light switches, a touchscreen display for monitoring power and water, and switches for the water system.
All in all, the Koa packs all most people need to hit the road in comfort and style. The cherry on top is that the rig can keep its occupants on the road for longer periods thanks to its off-grid-ready setup. By the way, this van is built on the company's Drifter model, but it has a few additions.
As mentioned in the title, Koa is looking for a new owner. According to the listing by Beachside Custom Vans , its price tag is $144,500 (€129,240). The vehicle has just 400 miles (644 km), which is basically brand-new for a camper van. The company also offers a 2-year Beachside builder warranty.
